s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, progressive, cutaneous vascular lesions with erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques
salient_findings: Multiple, slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques
Firm, nonscaly, purple erythematous patches and plaques with irregular borders
Thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels dispersed between thickened collagen bundles
key_facts: Female patient in her late 20s
2-year history of skin lesions
Lesions located on left upper arm, left axilla, and lateral thoracic region
No triggers such as local infection, insect bite, or trauma occurred before lesion appearance
No fever, weight loss, or fatigue
No extracutaneous involvement observed
Histopathological examination showed irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels
Endothelial cells were plump but displayed no significant cytologic atypia
Immunohistochemistry results positive for CD31, CD34, Ki-67 (<1%)
Immunohistochemistry results negative for podoplanin (D2-40) and human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8)

shortlist.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological examination showed irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels, and immunohistochemistry results were positive for CD31 and CD34, which are consistent with Kaposi's sarcoma

shortlist.label: Tufted angioma
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques, and histopathological examination showed irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels

shortlist.label: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical and histopathological features to Kaposi's sarcoma, and immunohistochemistry results were positive for CD31 and CD34

shortlist.label: Retiform hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological examination showed irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels, and clinical presentation of slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques

shortlist.label: Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques, and histopathological examination showed irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques with irregular borders, combined with the histopathological findings of irregularly branched, thin-walled blood vessels and positive immunohistochemistry results for CD31 and CD34, is most consistent with retiform hemangioendothelioma.

rejected.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
rejected.why: Negative immunohistochemistry results for human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) and lack of systemic symptoms or extracutaneous involvement make Kaposi's sarcoma less likely.

rejected.label: Tufted angioma
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and histopathological findings do not match the characteristic tufted or cannonball pattern of blood vessels seen in tufted angioma.

rejected.label: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma
rejected.why: The absence of significant cytologic atypia and the negative immunohistochemistry results for podoplanin (D2-40) make kaposiform hemangioendothelioma less likely.

rejected.label: Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and histopathological findings do not match the characteristic targetoid appearance and hemosiderin deposition seen in targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma.
